title: The Ad Skills: Script, Record, Edit, Statics, Set Up
lede: Jarvis writes the scripts, you film them, Jarvis edits them, makes the statics and sets the campaign up with you. One order, every time.
deliverable: Video ads, static ads and a Meta campaign ready to turn on.
body:
Five steps in a fixed order, with you in the middle holding the phone: Jarvis writes the scripts, you film them, Jarvis edits them, makes the statics, then walks you through setting the campaign up inside Meta. If Jarvis says a skill is missing, go back to How Ads Actually Work and install this module’s skills first.

The order

StepWho does itWhat comes out
1. ScriptAd Scripting skillFive to ten video scripts, each on a different angle, 30 to 60 seconds
2. RecordYou and your phoneEach script filmed, a few takes, best take picked
3. EditAd Editing skillEach take cut to the hook, captioned, three cuts per script
4. StaticsStatic Ad Creator skillImage ads on the same angles, for people who do not watch video
5. Set upMeta Campaign Setup skillOne campaign, one ad set, one ad per angle, named, budgeted, with a check schedule

Step 1: scripting

The Ad Scripting skill takes your offer, your market research and where your buyer sits on the awareness ladder, and turns them into scripts you read to camera. Every script tests one angle and says which one in its heading, so when one wins you know why.

Run the Ad Scripting skill. My offer: [paste your six line offer]. My market research: [paste the brief from the offer module]. My buyer is mostly [problem aware / solution aware] about this. Write me eight video ad scripts, each 30 to 60 seconds, each testing a different angle: the costly problem, the desired result, the main objection, how the system works, and proof I actually have. Hook in the first three seconds, spoken plain language the way I talk on a call, name the exact kind of business owner in the first line, and end every script with the same call to action to my booking page. Label each script with the angle it tests. No price, no invented results, no made up testimonials.

Read them out loud. Cut any line you would never say to a real owner on the phone. If a script needs a number you do not have, delete the number. Pick the five you believe in most and film those.

Step 2: filming

Just film a talking head video. Your phone, decent light, you talking to one owner the way you talk on a call. I show you how I do mine in the video. The ads that work for this offer are a real person saying a real thing, not a production.

Examples that work. Blake adds his winning ad examples here.

Once you have a winning angle, come back with this prompt. It gives you five versions of the same script so you can re-film the winner without starting again.

This script is winning: [paste the script and the numbers it is getting]. Give me five versions of it. Keep the angle and the call to action exactly the same. Change one thing per version: a new opening line, a different story in the middle, a different objection handled, a shorter cut, and a version I can film somewhere else. Label each change.

Step 3: editing

The Ad Editing skill takes your best take and makes it an ad. It cuts straight to the hook inside two seconds, adds captions because most people watch with the sound off, trims the dead air, and gives you three cuts of every script with different openings. One filming session becomes three ads to test.

The Ad Editing skill is being finished. Until it lands, open the clip in CapCut, turn on auto captions, and cut everything before your first strong line.

Step 4: statics

Some buyers never watch a video in the feed. Static ads catch them. The Static Ad Creator skill works from the same angles as your scripts, makes callout, proof, scene and carousel formats, and shows you each one at phone size before you upload it.

Run the Static Ad Creator skill. Use my offer [paste] and these two winning angles from my scripts [paste the two scripts]. Make me three static ad concepts per angle that test a real difference, not three recolours. For each one give me the image copy, the primary text, the headline and the call to action to my booking page. No price, no invented results, no fake screenshots. Render them and show me each one at feed size so I can pick.

Pick two or three. If it would not stop you mid scroll, it will not stop them.

Examples that work. Blake adds his winning static examples here.

Step 5: setting the campaign up

This is the part people pay a media buyer for and do not need to. One campaign, one ad set, broad targeting by country, one ad per angle. The words do the targeting. The Meta Campaign Setup skill tells you what to click, step by step, and gives you the names, a starting budget worked out from your ticket, and what to check at 24 hours, 72 hours and 7 days.

Run the Meta Campaign Setup skill. My offer sells at [price]. My four numbers: most I will spend to win one client [number], most one qualified booked call can cost [number], most one lead can cost [number]. I have [number] video ads and [number] static ads ready, on these angles: [list]. My booking page is [link]. My country is [country]. Walk me through setting this up in Meta as one campaign with one ad set and one ad per angle, tell me what to click at each step, give me the naming convention, the daily budget to start with and why, and the exact checks to do at 24 hours, 72 hours and 7 days with the scale, fix or kill rule for each.

Meta moves its buttons around. Where the skill does not match your screen, describe what you see to Jarvis. Do not turn the campaign on until your booking page is live and you have tested it yourself on your phone.

Where every ad sends people

Your booking page, with the qualifying questions and the follow up behind it. An ad that sends people to a home page, a DM, or a form with no follow up is money set on fire.

My rules that never bend

  • No price in any ad, image or page. The price is agreed on a call, against the cost of their problem.
  • No invented results. No result yet, lead with the problem and the mechanism. Your first real result becomes your proof ad.
  • No fake testimonials, screenshots or urgency.
  • Keep a record. Every ad gets a line in your CRM: angle, spend, cost per qualified call, decision, reason.
